title: He Sendeth Sun, He Sendeth Shower
description: He Sendeth Sun, He Sendeth Shower in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Sarah Flower Adams wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 264, “Thy Will Be Done!”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: He sen-deth sun, He sen-deth shower; A-like they're need-ful for the flower; And joys and tears a-like are sent To give the soul fit nour-ish-ment: As comes to me or cloud or sun, Fa-ther, Thy will, not mine, be done!

lines: He sendeth sun, He sendeth shower;
Alike they're needful for the flower;
And joys and tears alike are sent
To give the soul fit nourishment:
As comes to me or cloud or sun,
Father, Thy will, not mine, be done!
With murmurs whom they trust and love?
A trusting, loving child to Thee
As comes to me or cloud or sun,
Father, Thy will, not mine, be done!
O, ne'er will I at life repine!
Enough that Thou hast made it mine.
When falls the shadow cold of death,
I yet will sing, with parting breath, —
As comes to me or shade or sun,
Father, Thy will, not mine, be done!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Sarah Flower Adams died in 1848.
credits: Words by Sarah Flower Adams (1805–1848), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
